current.title: The Third Visitor From Outside Our Solar System
current.hook: Something from deep space just blasted past your planet at 246,000 kilometers an hour.
current.closing: Three visitors, ever. Each one bigger.
current.question: Will we ever catch one? Tell me.

segments.say: We've confirmed visitors from outside our solar system just 3 times: 2017, 2019, then 2025.
Each was faster: 'Oumuamua 140,000 kilometers an hour, Borisov 177,000, 3I/ATLAS 246,000.
Biggest yet: 3I/ATLAS's nucleus could span 5.6 kilometers, versus Borisov's 1.

held_for: judge: A story about a comet passing at 246,000 km/h is told entirely with bar charts and bare numbers, and no visitor, rock or motion through space ever appears on screen.
reasons: judge: A story about a comet passing at 246,000 km/h is told entirely with bar charts and bare numbers, and no visitor, rock or motion through space ever appears on screen.

judge.one_line: A story about a comet passing at 246,000 km/h is told entirely with bar charts and bare numbers, and no visitor, rock or motion through space ever appears on screen.
problems: The hook (hook@0.3 to hook@2.2) is a static 1-2-3 count bar chart while the narration says 246,000 km/h. Nothing blasts past, and frame one gives no reason to stay.
The seg0 chart is identical to the hook's, so the opening ~4.5s is one picture.
At seg2:end cyan circles cover the 177K and 140K labels and Data's head covers 246K.
seg3 shows nucleus size as two numbers beside two mascots, with no sense of scale.
seg4 shows the difference '4.6 apart' on a ruler, which doesn't prove 'each one bigger', and the closing claims three sizes while only two were shown.
Data points, cheers or stands beside the marks in every scene and never causes the motion.
fixes: Open on the finished shock: a lit comet streaking past Earth with a speed trail and the single headline 246,000 km/h on screen from frame one.
Show speed as three comets racing across a starfield, with Data launching or chasing each one, instead of a bar race. Remove the circle overlays from the labels.
Redraw seg3 as two nuclei at true 1:5.6 scale, with the small one ghosted onto the big one.
Make the closing three rocks lined up and growing, with Data stacking them, so 'each one bigger' is visible.
Fill the frame: put the subject in the hero band and leave no empty dark gradient above or below it.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.

PACE: each SAY is ONE spoken sentence of at most 16 words — the number and what it means, nothing else; the HOOK at most 14 words, the CLOSING at most 10, the QUESTION at most 8. A beat is on screen about 8 seconds; a longer line is refused. Each SAY says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
